own_solution.law: The receding panel receives frequency f(c-w)/c. Reflection preserves frequency in the panel frame, so the reflected frequency received by the retreating recorder is f_received = f(c-w)(c-v)/[c(c+w)]. Thus the decrease is f-f_received. Carrying the recorder away along the deck replaces v with v+q.
assumptions: The stated constant velocities are relative to the still air.
Walking speeds along the deck are relative to the trolley.
The recorder travels with the trolley unless the added sentence specifies that it is carried.
Reflection preserves frequency in the panel frame, as stated.

notes: All certified answers agree with the Doppler relations. Recorder walking speeds of 1.1, 1.6 and 2.4 m/s give decreases of 94.2263, 96.3377 and 99.7160 Hz. The supplied crest-arrival relations are dimensionally and physically correct; subtracting successive arrival times eliminates the initial separation at every listed distance. Prescribed trolley speed prevents toolbox motion from changing recorder speed. The explicitly claimed numerical minimal pairs preserve 1.6 m/s and change only the intended attachment or event.
